title: SYSK's Halloween Scare Fest
summary: Halloween special in which Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant read two public-domain horror short stories by candlelight and brandy in their study. The first is "The Striding Place" by Gertrude Atherton (originally titled "The Twins"), about a man who tries to rescue his missing friend Wyatt Gifford from a treacherous river rapid called the Strid in Yorkshire, only to find the body has no face. The second is "The Pale Man" by Julius Long (from Weird Tales, vol. 24, no. 3), about an assistant professor at a country hotel who is pursued room by room by a pale stranger who turns out to be nonexistent. The hosts briefly discuss Weird Tales magazine, Gertrude Atherton's nickname "Old Gert," and the Strid, and wrap up with Halloween greetings.

segments.title: Halloween opening and setup
segments.summary: Hosts open the Halloween episode by the fireplace, with a stormy night, brandy, and Reese's pieces, and decide to split reading two short stories this year.

segments.name: The Striding Place
segments.title: The Striding Place by Gertrude Atherton
segments.summary: Read aloud: Weagle searches for his missing friend Wyatt Gifford, recalls a conversation about the soul lingering after death, and sees a hand in the foam of the Strid. He rescues the body with a branch, but the body has no face. Hosts discuss the story's origin as 'The Twins' and the Strid in Yorkshire.

segments.name: Weird Tales and The Pale Man introduction
segments.title: Introducing Weird Tales and The Pale Man
segments.summary: Hosts describe Weird Tales as a Chicago pulp magazine started in 1923 that published HP Lovecraft, and introduce 'The Pale Man' by Julius Long.

segments.name: The Pale Man by Julius Long
segments.title: The Pale Man by Julius Long
segments.summary: Read aloud: an assistant professor on vacation at a country hotel is obsessed with a pale stranger who keeps moving to rooms closer to his. Neighbors die, the narrator falls ill, and the room clerk says no such guest exists. The story ends with the door opening. Hosts compare the pale man to Slender Man.

segments.name: Outro and Halloween sign-off
segments.title: Halloween sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts pour more brandy, wish each other and Jerry a happy Halloween, and urge listeners to be safe.

segments.name: Closing credits
segments.title: Closing credits
segments.summary: Standard HowStuffWorks closing line directing listeners to the website.
